## Load all my listening stats

### (2013 onwards)

```{r}
#load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)
library(lubridate)
library(dygraphs)
```

```{{r}}
|# cache: true
data <- list.files("any_topic_files/spotify_data/",
                      pattern = "\\.json$",
                      full.names = TRUE)

spotify <- data |>
  map(\(f) fromJSON(f, flatten = TRUE)) |>
  bind_rows()

#check
glimpse(spotify)
```

```{r}
spotify <- spotify |>
  transmute(
    ts         = ymd_hms(ts),
    year       = year(ts),
    ms_played  = ms_played,
    minutes    = ms_played / 60000,
    titel      = master_metadata_track_name,
    artist  = master_metadata_album_artist_name,
    album      = master_metadata_album_album_name,
    skipped, shuffle, offline, platform,
    reason_start, reason_end
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(titel))   # delete Podcasts 
```

```{r}
my_fav_s <- spotify |>
  count(titel, artist, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

fav_artist_per_year <- spotify |>
  group_by(year, artist) |>
  summarise(hours = sum(minutes) / 60, .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(year) |>
  slice_max(hours, n = 1)



```

## Interactive Table

```{r}
#| echo: false


library(DT)
table_tbl <- spotify |>
  select(year, minutes, titel, artist)|>
  group_by(titel, artist)|>
  summarise(hours = sum(minutes) / 60, .groups = "drop") |> 
  filter(hours >= 1)

table_tbl |>
  datatable(options = list(pageLength = 25))
```

This table shows the title, the artist and how many hours I listened to that song during all years I used Spotify.

## My favourite artist of all time

```{r}
#executed but not displayed R-code

fav_artist_alltime <- spotify |>
  group_by(artist) |>
  summarise(hours = sum(minutes) / 60) |>
  slice_max(hours, n = 10) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hours, y = reorder(artist, hours))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1DB954") +
  labs(x = "Time (hours)", y = NULL,
       title = "My favourite artists of all time") +
  theme_minimal()

(fav_artist_alltime)
```

## How many hours did I listen to per month? 

```{r}

spotify <- spotify |>
  mutate(month = floor_date(ts, "month") |> as_date())

monthly_hours <- spotify |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(hours = sum(minutes) / 60, .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(month = seq(min(month), max(month), by = "month"),
           fill = list(hours = 0))

```

```{r}
#| echo: false
dygraph(monthly_hours, main = "Amount of hours listening to music", ylab = "hours")

```

## Shuffle Mode ON 
### The Fisher- Yates Shuffle Technique

$$
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
&\text{Input: } A \text{ is a sequence of } n \text{ symbols} \\[2mm]
&\textbf{For } i = n-1 \text{ down to } 1 \textbf{ Do} \\
&\hspace{1cm} T[i] = \text{random number } j \in [0,i] \\
&\textbf{End For} \\[2mm]
&\textbf{For } i = n-1 \text{ down to } 1 \textbf{ Do} \\
&\hspace{1cm} j = T[i] \\
&\hspace{1cm} \textbf{If } j \neq i \textbf{ Then} \\
&\hspace{2cm} B = A[j] \\
&\hspace{2cm} A[j] = A[i] \\
&\hspace{2cm} A[i] = B \\
&\hspace{1cm} \textbf{End If} \\
&\textbf{End For}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
$$

[Find out more here](https://codezup.com/spotify-shuffle-algorithm-not-random/)

## Motivation Music

I do not only like to listen to music; I also love to do sports. Listening to music makes my runs easier. This subjective feeling is supported by meta-analytical results which show that listening to music while exercising enhances enjoyment and reduces the perceived exertion [@terry_effects_2020].
